What the numbers say

For the session of Wednesday, November 11, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (36 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as neutral. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is sideways and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

18 of 36 tickers (50%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 21 of 34 (62%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 27 rose and 9 fell; the median move was +2.38%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Technology had the strongest average move at +6.40% and Healthcare the weakest at −0.60%, a spread of 7.00 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 2.54 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

1 ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (NVDA), and 1 at or above 70 (COST). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-10), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 28% to 50%, and the regime reading changed from risk-off to neutral.
